inicio.kicker: FTH — Humanoid Technology Training · course 2 of 5 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: From simulator to ground: sim-to-real in humanoids
inicio.lead: A walking policy that walks in the simulator and falls on the robot. In eight lessons you measure that gap, test randomization, identify the actuator, measure the latency, fix the simulator with data, run the policy through a sim2sim gate with DDS, and build the ladder to the ground. All on CPU, no robot.
inicio.capa_alt: Industrial humanoid robot standing on the floor of a dark lab, held to a gantry by a slack cable, with a simulation monitor in the background and the title From simulator to ground.

numeros.t: steps in the sim2sim gate (with DDS)

inicio.aulas_sub: From the measured gap to the deployment ladder: randomization, system identification, actuator latency, fixing with data, sim2sim, real-to-sim, and the plan to the ground.

itens: You program in Python, have seen ROS 2 (or took the robot course), and want to bring a humanoid policy to the robot.
If you don't have a humanoid: the "real robot" in the practice sessions is a MuJoCo with hidden parameters, and we say so openly.
You took course 0 (the ~/fth bench) and course 1 (locomotion with RL), or you want to start from a ready-made policy.

blocos.t: What you walk away able to do
itens: Measure the gap of a ready-made policy and find which parameters knock it down.
Read the randomization ranges from a real training run and test inside and outside them.
Identify the actuator's kp with the mujoco.sysid toolbox and measure the latency on the bench.
Run the policy through a sim2sim gate with another model and DDS, and write the ladder to the ground.
